context.concept_name: Remove model-serving resources safely on an existing platform

coverage.learning_objective: Remove only verified exclusively retired resources while preserving active service, artifacts and secret-safe records.

required_facts.statement: Authorize cleanup against the retired-resource inventory and permitted identity scope, preserving the active release rather than selecting resources by age alone.
Inspect actual container labels and compare ownership and release/version metadata with the approved active and retired inventory.
source_refs: docker_docs#https://docs.docker.com/engine/manage-resources/labels/ — Label keys and values; Manage labels on objects

required_facts.statement: Inspect each candidate container’s identity and State.Running/exit state; inspect its logs and associated compute lifecycle before deciding it is exclusively retired.
Check captured commands and logs for secret values or sensitive data, with runtime-injected credentials kept out of cleanup code and printed output.
source_refs: docker_docs#https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/use-secrets/ — Manage secrets securely in Docker Compose (introductory paragraphs on environment-variable exposure and secrets printed in debug logs); Use secrets

docker_docs#https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/secrets/ — Example: Rotate a secret (command reads passwords from /run/secrets without exposing them on the command line or saving them in shell history)

google_mlops_pipelines#https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/create-secret-quickstart — Create a secret and access a secret version / Python (WARNING: Do not print the secret in a production environment)
docker_docs#https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/logs/ — Description (stdout/stderr retrieval; --details can include environment variables and labels)

required_facts.statement: Stop only a verified retired container with docker container stop NAME, then remove that stopped retired container with docker container rm NAME.
source_refs: docker_docs#https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/rm/ — Description; Remove a container; Remove all stopped containers

required_facts.statement: Terminate only the verified exclusively retired nonproduction instance with gcloud compute instances delete INSTANCE --zone=ZONE under the approved disk-preservation policy.
Preserve the active release’s referenced images and required model/preprocessing artifacts; removing a retired container is not authorization to delete shared artifacts.
source_refs: docker_docs#https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/image/pull/ — Pull an image by digest (immutable identifier)

required_facts.statement: Verify the active serving release remains healthy with a bounded readiness/prediction check, and inspect the inventory to confirm approved retired resources are absent.
Write one audit record containing verified ownership, active/retired identities, authorized actions, retained artifacts and credential non-disclosure checks.

Before the deletion in f6, use gcloud compute instances describe INSTANCE --zone=ZONE to inspect status and identity against the verified exclusively retired inventory; afterward verify the deletion operation completed successfully and repeat describe for the same project, zone and instance to check expected absence, accepting only a not-found response for that instance as absence evidence, not authentication, permission or other failures.
source_refs: google_mlops_pipelines#https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/deleting-instance — Delete an instance: client-library examples (wait for operation completion and check errors)

teaching_blocks.title: Control Workload Cost and Retire Resources
teaching_blocks.content: Retired resources can be cleaned up only after ownership and release status are verified. An old-looking container may still reference active artifacts, so age alone is not a safe authorization rule.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Authorize cleanup against the retired-resource inventory and permitted identity scope, preserving the active release rather than selecting resources by age alone. Inspect actual container labels and compare ownership and release/version metadata with the approved active and retired inventory. Inspect each candidate container’s identity and State.Running/exit state; inspect its logs and associated compute lifecycle before deciding it is exclusively retired.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Keep runtime-injected credentials in the authorized runtime secret mechanism, not in cleanup code or printed output. Check captured commands and logs for secret values or sensitive data. This non-disclosure check is supported by Docker’s [Manage secrets securely in Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/use-secrets/) (introductory guidance on exposure in debug logs; Use secrets), [SecretsUsedInArgOrEnv](https://docs.docker.com/reference/build-checks/secrets-used-in-arg-or-env/) (Description), and [Swarm secrets](https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/secrets/) (Example: Rotate a secret, which keeps passwords off the command line and out of shell history). Container-log retrieval alone does not establish the credential-handling rule. Stop only a verified retired container with docker container stop NAME, then remove that stopped retired container with docker container rm NAME. Terminate only the verified exclusively retired nonproduction instance with gcloud compute instances delete INSTANCE --zone=ZONE under the approved disk-preservation policy.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Preserve the active release’s referenced images and required model/preprocessing artifacts; removing a retired container is not authorization to delete shared artifacts. Verify the active serving release remains healthy with a bounded readiness/prediction check, and inspect the inventory to confirm approved retired resources are absent. Write one audit record containing verified ownership, active/retired identities, authorized actions, retained artifacts and credential non-disclosure checks.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Before deleting the verified exclusively retired nonproduction instance, use gcloud compute instances describe INSTANCE --zone=ZONE in the approved project to inspect its status and identity against the verified retired inventory. After the authorized deletion, wait for the deletion operation to complete and check that it completed successfully without errors. Then repeat describe for the same project, zone and instance. Accept only a not-found response for that specific instance as evidence of absence; authentication, permission or other failures are inconclusive or failed verification, not proof that the instance is gone.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content: Compare actual container labels, identities, running/exit state and logs with the approved active/retired inventory and compute lifecycle. Stop and remove only a verified retired container. Before deleting the exclusively retired nonproduction instance, describe it in the approved project and zone and check its status and identity against the verified retired inventory. Delete only that instance under the approved disk-preservation policy, wait for the deletion operation to complete and check that it succeeded without errors. Repeat describe for the same project, zone and instance: only that instance's not-found response establishes absence; authentication, permission or other failures leave verification inconclusive or failed. Preserve active image references and required model/preprocessing artifacts, even if retired containers also used them. Afterward, verify the active release's readiness and bounded prediction and inspect that the approved retired resources are absent. Write one audit record of ownership, authorized actions, retained artifacts and credential non-disclosure checks. Keep runtime-injected credentials in the authorized runtime secret mechanism and out of cleanup code and printed output; check captured commands and logs for secret values or sensitive data before including cleanup evidence in the audit record.

teaching_blocks.title: A distinction to keep
teaching_blocks.content: Removing a retired container is not authorization to delete shared artifacts. Cleanup follows verified ownership, permitted scope and lifecycle state while preserving the active serving release.

video_need.reason: A live fixture with visible intermediate state and acceptance checks would make this distinction concrete: Cleanup follows ownership and lifecycle state, not age alone.

practice_anchor.objective: Clean the supplied nonproduction serving-resource inventory using the authorized identity and runtime-injected credentials. Reconcile container labels, identities, running/exit state and logs, plus compute identity and lifecycle, with the approved active/retired inventory. Stop and remove only verified retired containers and delete only the exclusively retired test instance under the approved disk-preservation policy. Preserve active resources and required artifacts, verify health and absence, and deliver one safe-cleanup audit record.
practice_anchor.success: Only authorized, verified retired resources are removed. The compute deletion operation succeeds, and a repeated describe in the same project and zone returns not-found for that specific instance; other failures do not count as absence. The active release passes bounded readiness and prediction checks, its required images and artifacts remain, and one audit record documents ownership, identities, actions, retention and credential non-disclosure checks.

live_code.required_skill: Apply bounded cleanup commands only after reconciling approved inventory with runtime evidence, then verify safe outcomes and record sanitized evidence.
live_code.starter_state_intent: Provide an isolated, existing nonproduction runtime with approved active/retired identities, permitted identity scope, disk-preservation policy, runtime-injected credentials, shared required artifacts and supplied bounded health checks. Container and compute inspection evidence must be available; inventory age alone must not establish retirement. Use supplied resource names as NAME and INSTANCE and the approved zone as ZONE, with the approved project already selected.
live_code.observable_success: Captured actions show identity and lifecycle inspection before removal, stop before container removal, and compute describe before deletion. Deletion completes successfully, followed by a same-project, same-zone describe whose specific-instance not-found response establishes absence. Inventory inspection confirms retired containers are absent, bounded readiness/prediction checks pass, and required active artifacts remain. The single audit record contains verified ownership, active/retired identities, authorized actions, retained artifacts and checks that captured commands, logs and cleanup code disclose neither credentials nor sensitive data.

visual_anchor.purpose: Make the approved inventory and runtime evidence visible before cleanup, including container ownership labels, release identities, running/exit state and compute lifecycle. After cleanup, show retired-resource absence, successful compute deletion and specific-instance not-found evidence alongside retained active resources, required artifacts, bounded health results and sanitized audit evidence.
